fix(record_locks): keep quote-session selectors compatible with labels (#8724)

Closes #8724

## What changes

The enterprise quote-session scenario finds line-name and adjustment-label inputs by their exact placeholders within their dialogs. These queries continue to identify the intended controls when #8705 supplies real accessible labels. Only two selectors change; every assertion, fixture, cleanup step, timeout and retry setting remains intact. No production code or contribution guard changes.

## Validation

Runner: local. The managed enterprise quote-session scenario passes both P0 and P1 against main-derived code. It also passes with all 13 changed files from #8705 at `31a4282a35b549929e142eb84f9871edc36ef8a6` temporarily applied: P0 conversion/totals/locks 8.8s; P1 stale-session protection 3.4s. Every temporary source overlay was restored. The four-case browser selector matrix passes both label states with decoy controls; the old selectors fail with associated labels.

Package build, generate, rebuild, typecheck, i18n sync/usage, app build, template parity and 13 contribution-guard tests passed. The actual base-pinned enterprise contribution guard and CLA check pass. The initial default full unit run failed eight temporary-root assertions in unchanged CLI suites. All three suites pass directly (33 tests), and the complete CLI suite passes both serially and through Turbo with `TMPDIR=/tmp` preserved (`114 suites / 2352 tests`). The complete workspace unit rerun with `TMPDIR=/tmp yarn test --env-mode=loose` passed: **51/51 tasks**, 5m29s. No CLI or runner configuration was changed; the temporary-directory normalization applies only to this local invocation.

#8705 remains a separate PR; this verifies its quote-session compatibility, not its unrelated findings. Independent native approval and required CI remain merge gates. No remote merge performed.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(frontend): give the detail page its own attachments pagination

## What

The publication detail page now keeps its own page number for the unlabeled attachments, starting at 1, instead of using the global pagination context.

## Why

The global pagination context holds the landing page's current results page. The detail page used it in two ways:

- **Starting page:** it used that value as the first page of its attachments pager. Opening a publication from results page 2 or later requested that page of the attachments (`_page=2`, offset 50), which is empty for nearly every publication, so the "Bijlagen" row disappeared. After a hard refresh it worked, because the in-memory context resets to page 1.
- **Writing back:** it wrote its attachments page back into the context, so paging through attachments changed which results page "Back to homepage" opened.

## Changes

- `WOOItemDetailTemplate.tsx`: the attachments page is now local state starting at 1; the `usePaginationContext` usage and the `useEffect` that wrote the page back are removed.

The landing page still uses the global context, so returning from a publication still opens the same results page.

Keep a refused run's follower in a description or footnote + body Follow-up to carve-js#4449 (markup-carve/carve#5195). The line after a refused brace run continues its paragraph whatever it opens (CARVE-P2-035). Where a `+` attached such a run to a description or a footnote, carve-js still ended the attached block at a list marker on the next line, so the marker left the host as a new list. This held for attribute runs on main already; since #4449 a refused `{%` run reads the same way, so the comment form showed the gap too. ## Results ``` :: t : d + {x } - b ``` Before: ```html
t

d

{x }

  • b
``` After (the spec model's output): ```html
t

d

{x } - b

``` The same holds for `{% x` / `%}` and for a footnote host (`[^n]: x` / `+` / run / `- b`). A sibling still ends its host first, as the model reads it: `- a` / `+` / `{x` / `}` / `- b` keeps `b` as the next item, and `: e` after the run is the next description. ## How `collectAttachedBlock` stops at the caller's boundary unless the lines collected so far are one refused brace run (`isRefusedBraceRun`, a run starting at the block's first line whose continuation sits at or left of its `{`). Item hosts, and a description, term or footnote marker on the follower line, keep the old boundary. The run check only runs when a boundary is hit. ## Variants 13,440 generated documents (14 hosts with and without `+`, including descriptions, footnotes, quotes and nested items; eight comment and attribute run shapes with the continuation at columns 0 to 3; 15 followers including sibling items, descriptions, notes, quotes and fences), compared with the spec model at carve main: main 12,920 agree, this branch 12,968, regressions 0. ## Timing `carveToHtml` on a document of these shapes (load about 17 on 12 cores, so the numbers are noisy): 2k 276 to 201 ms, 8k 312 to 275 ms, 32k 694 to 796 ms. The new check runs at most twice per attached block. ## Review codex review (medium): no introduced defect found; it read `parse-session.ts` and `parse-prepass-core.ts` and ran the targeted tests.

Artifact upload size check off-by-one

## Summary
The upload size check used `>=` against `MAX_FILE_SIZE_IN_BYTES` (8e6), rejecting files of exactly 8mb even though the limit is documented as "8mb".

## Changes
- `src/controllers/api/artifact.storage.controller.ts`
  - `>=` changed to `>` so files up to and including 8mb are accepted.
  - Validation message corrected to "Max file size limit is 8mb!".

## Verification
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npx eslint src/controllers/api/artifact.storage.controller.ts` passes

benchmarks.task_description: Handle escaped and mid-paragraph `$$` math in the Markdown editor ## References Follow-up to #19903 (part of #19816), covering the remaining notes from its reviews: the mid-line case from https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/pull/19903#pullrequestreview-5429465259 and escaped delimiters. ## Code changes In `packages/codemirror/src/extensions/ipython-md.ts`, on top of #19903 as merged: - `opensMathBlock` finds the `$$` delimiters with the existing `mathDelimiters` scan, which skips backslash escapes and code spans, so `$$ x \$$` opens a math block instead of being taken as opened and closed on the same line. - The closing `$$` of a math block is found with the same scan, so an escaped `\$$` inside the block does not close it. - While a paragraph has `$$` math that is still open, ~~the other leaf parsers are~~ the setext heading parser is held back on each setext underline, so in `Some text $$` / `a` / `=` / `$$` the `=` line is not read as a setext underline. ## Testing ~~Three~~ Ten new cases in `packages/codemirror/test/mathparser.spec.ts`~~, one per change~~; each fails on `main` and passes here. > **Added by a maintainer** > > Two more cases check that a table with `$$` in a cell keeps its structure, also when GFM is configured after the math extension. ## User-facing changes In Markdown cells and files, the editor highlights these `$$` math blocks as LaTeX instead of breaking them up or turning their lines into headings. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | > **Added by a maintainer** > > A setext heading whose text has an unpaired `$$`, such as `Making $$ with Python` over a line of `=`, is now shown as a paragraph in the editor, as an unclosed `$$` at the start of a line already is. The rendered cell still shows a heading. ## Backwards-incompatible changes None. ## AI usage - **YES**: Some of the content of this PR was generated by AI. - **YES**: The human author has carefully reviewed this PR and run this code. AI tools used: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
